title: KV Cache Compression by Estimating Future Queries Distribution
one_line_claim: Expected Attention estimates future query distributions analytically to compress KV caches without training.
method_summary: Expected Attention leverages Gaussian properties of LLM hidden states and RoPE positional embeddings to analytically estimate future query distributions without training. For each KV pair, the method computes an expected contribution score as the integral of its interaction with all possible future queries; KV pairs are ranked and lowest-scoring pairs pruned to achieve target compression ratios.

key_findings.finding: Expected Attention achieves up to 60% KV cache compression while maintaining performance on long-context benchmarks.
key_findings.quote: Expected Attention achieves 50% and 90% cache compression while reducing the KV cache size by 2x with performance parity.

key_findings.finding: Operates during both prefilling and decoding without requiring training or task-specific tuning.
key_findings.quote: Training-free compression method that can be applied to any pretrained model

key_findings.finding: Outperforms SnapKV, TOVA, and KeyDiff baselines on LongBench across Llama, Qwen, Gemma.
key_findings.quote: Figure 2 shows Expected Attention achieves optimal compression-performance trade-offs on LongBench

relation_to_herald.shared: Both address KV cache compression as a critical bottleneck and operate at inference time without retraining; both evaluate on Llama and Qwen models.
differs_on: Expected Attention uses analytical estimation of future query distributions; HERALD uses supervised learning (XGBoost) on per-token logit features to predict failure.
Expected Attention is itself a compression method; HERALD is a failure detector for any compression method treated as a black box.
Expected Attention optimizes the compression-quality tradeoff; HERALD detects catastrophic failures (looping, non-termination) that occur during aggressive compression.
